paragraphs: Friend, here's the heart of it. Shimei had cursed David and thrown stones at him when David fled Jerusalem (2 Samuel 16:5-13). Now David is king again, and Shimei falls down and says, "I have sinned" (2 Samuel 19:20). Abishai says what sounds fair: "Shouldn't Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD's anointed?" (2 Samuel 19:21).

And David says no. He asks, "Should any man be put to death in Israel today?" and then tells him, "You shall not die" (2 Samuel 19:22-23). I think that's a king with all the power in the world choosing mercy, and the BSB says he swore an oath to it. Mercy was in David's hands, and he gave it away on purpose. Don't miss that, baker, because some of us want to hold a grudge like it's the last cookie in the box!

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery. When someone owns what they did, you get to decide what you do with the power you have. Mercy isn't pretending it didn't happen. It's looking at someone who says "I have sinned" and letting them live. I know how it feels to be set aside and forgotten, so believe me, I love a story where somebody gets mercy instead of the hammer. And this story isn't over, friend, so keep that apron on.
